heroSummary: The Bambu Lab P1S handles eSUN PETG out of the box with outstanding reliability using the stock direct-drive extruder and stainless steel nozzle. By locking the volumetric flow rate to 14 mm³/s, the system achieves a reliable safe maximum print speed of 167 mm/s without sacrificing layer bonding or surface quality.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate (clean with dish soap; glue stick recommended strictly as a release agent to prevent surface damage)
slicerTweaks: Set Filament Max Volumetric Speed to 14 mm³/s in OrcaSlicer to prevent under-extrusion at high feedrates.
Disable the Auxiliary Part Cooling Fan completely (set to 0%) to prevent asymmetric warping and differential shrinkage.
Calibrate Pressure Advance (PA) in OrcaSlicer, setting the direct-drive baseline to approximately 0.036 for crisp corners without blobbing.
Enable 'Wipe while retracting' (2 mm wipe distance) and set Z-hop to 0.4 mm Spiral to eliminate PETG nozzle accumulation and wisps.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Hairy stringing and fine whisker buildup on travel moves
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: PETG is highly hygroscopic and absorbs ambient moisture quickly, causing steam micro-explosions and nozzle drool.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Dry the filament spool in a dedicated dryer at 65°C for 6 to 8 hours before printing, and keep retraction at 0.8 mm at 30 mm/s.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Over-adhesion and build plate coating tear-out
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: PETG chemically bonds strongly to PEI coatings when printed at high bed temperatures without an interface layer.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Apply a thin, even layer of liquid glue or PVP glue stick as a sacrificial release agent, and ensure the bed cools below 35°C before removing parts.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Weak layer bonding and matte chalky exterior finish
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Part cooling fan running too high or volumetric flow exceeding 14 mm³/s, chilling the melt pool before fusion.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Cap part cooling fan speed to a maximum of 50%, turn off the auxiliary cooling fan, and print outer walls at 240°C.

faq.question: Do I need to leave the P1S glass top or door open when printing eSUN PETG?
faq.answer: No, PETG has a higher glass transition temperature (~75°C to 80°C) than PLA, so leaving the chamber fully closed will not induce heat creep during standard print jobs.

faq.question: Should I upgrade the stock stainless steel nozzle on the P1S for eSUN PETG?
faq.answer: No upgrade is necessary because standard eSUN PETG is non-abrasive; the stock stainless steel hotend effortlessly withstands the required 240°C printing temperature.

faq.question: Why is the auxiliary chamber fan causing my PETG parts to warp on the P1S?
faq.answer: The auxiliary fan directs cold air unilaterally across the build plate, introducing uneven thermal contraction in PETG; it should be set to 0% in OrcaSlicer.

faq.question: Can I push eSUN PETG beyond 167 mm/s on the Bambu Lab P1S?
faq.answer: You can only increase speed if you decrease layer height or line width; at 0.2mm layer height and 0.42mm extrusion width, 167 mm/s represents the hard physical boundary of the 14 mm³/s hotend melt capacity.
